David de Meij, Nicolas Brown, Nataliia Bazaka

GitHub repository https://github.com/daviddemeij/pherc0306b-partial-letters-w040 — commit 9aee0e66f3 (2026-11-04). Documents: README.md, reader-v3-screen/README.md. Community code repository (Vesuvius Challenge), not peer reviewed; all figures self-reported by the authors. Images omitted.

File: README.md

PHerc. 0306B, winding w040: a row of letters, with segments, labels and predictions

Team: David de Meij, Nicolas Brown, Nataliia Bazaka.

We found a row of letters on winding w040 of PHerc. 0306B, in the lower block of the scan (z 6912– 9216, scan 20250521133212, 8.64 µm). This repository releases everything needed to check it, reuse it or build on it:

Segments: the w040 surface the letters sit on; the next winding's surface (w041), which continues the same sheet to the right; and an independent ScrollFiesta reconstruction of the letter row. Labels: five human-marked letters (two sure, three uncertain), with exact boxes. Predictions: raw Reader v3 ink probabilities at seven depths, on both faces, for the letter row and its continuations to the left and right. Both a single-depth and a depth-combined map are included. Figures: the stitched row in reading orientation, with raw-probability views and a blind-face control.

The letters

The labels were marked by a human (David de Meij) on Reader v3 depth-0 maps on 22 October 2026. They are observations, not model output.

Letter Confidence Box (w040 flat px, x0 y0 x1 y1) Size (mm, w × h)

The 3-D centre of the marked area is (x, y, z) = (5166, 4399, 8345) voxels. Boxes are in

labels/letters.json, and in the figure's frame in labels/letters_in_figure.json.

More ink in the same row. Left of χ, and on the w041 continuation 1.5–3 cm right of γ, the same row carries more ink. It is fainter and more fragmented, and we have not labelled it. The w041 side also shows blobs on the blind face, so read it with that control in mind.

Layout

segments/ w040.tifxyz, w041.tifxyz tifxyz (x/y/z.tif, meta.json); one node = 20 voxels rebuild_Wa_p002.tifxyz independent ScrollFiesta reconstruction (1 node per voxel) labels/ letters.json, letters_in_figure.json predictions/ w040-letters/ w040-left/ w041-right/ rebuild-Wa_p002/ (d0, both faces) readerv3_d{-4..+2}.tif, readerv3_d{..}_blind.tif raw Reader v3, uint8 (255 = probability 1) readerv3_depthpair.tif, readerv3_depthpair_blind.tif README.json frame (flat-px origin), window, model and volume pins figures/ PHerc0306B_w040-letters.png, panel_A..E.png, stitch.json code/ stitch_w040.py, make_w040_figure.py, depthpair.py, select_w040.py, remote_w040.sh, render_w040.py

How it was made

1. Surface. w040 and w041 are windings from a lasagna spiral fit (villa fit_spiral) of the z 6912–9216 block, flattened and snapped to the organisers' m7 surface prediction. 2. The fit exports one mesh per winding, cut at a fixed angle around the scroll axis. That cut is why w040 ends just after γ; the same sheet continues as w041. 3. At w040's right edge, w041 matches it with a median residual of about 2 voxels (18 µm). 4. In the figure, w041 is placed by one integer translation of (5466, 187) flat px. There is no warping or blending, and a gap of about 0.3 mm remains at the join. 5. Rendering. 66 layers along the surface normal, 1 voxel apart, sampled from level 0 of the public masked volume. 6. Ink. Reader v3 (HF domenicor046/reader-v3 @aee1d64, sha256 ea405417…) at depth offsets −4 to +2 voxels. It was run on both faces: reading, and blind (reversed layer order). 7. Depth pair. The depth at which ink is clearest varies along the row, so we keep, per pixel, the best mean of two adjacent depths. A stroke seen at two neighbouring depths keeps its strength; a blob seen at one depth is halved. Before pairing, each depth is averaged over 8 flips/transposes at d−2, d0 and d+1. The same rule runs on the blind face as a control (code/depthpair.py). 8. Display. Light yellow over the mean of CT layers 31–35, dimmed to 32 %, with no threshold. The figure also shows the raw score in grey at 0–1 and windowed to 0.30–0.75.

Checks

Independent surface reconstruction. We rebuilt the letter row from scratch, independent of the spiral fit: fresh Socratic sheet predictions, then ScrollFiesta cube meshing and assembly. The rebuilt piece lies a median 1.4 voxels from w040. On it, Reader v3 shows the same letters at the same places, and its blind face is nearly empty.

Blind-face control. On the blind face, the same rule shows scattered blobs but none of the row's letter shapes (panel D).

Reading orientation. This was checked geometrically. In w040's flat frame, z increases downwards and the winding angle around the scroll axis increases to the right, the same as on our W073 page, whose reading was confirmed independently. The images are shown unrotated. Sheet placement, from the CT profile along the normal in papyrus without ink around each letter: our sheet lies within 1–4 voxels of the surface; the neighbouring sheets lie 11–13 voxels inwards and 17–20 voxels outwards; the strokes are brightest on the outer face of our sheet, at +3 to +9 voxels.

This is consistent with the ink being on w040's own sheet. χ, at about half the distance to the outer neighbour, is the least certain.

Limits

Five letters, three of them uncertain. This is not a reading. We make no claim about the text. The right continuation is not a new surface. It is the existing w041 surface, translated once. Our ScrollFiesta reconstruction of the join found the neighbouring sheet there (about 10–15 voxels away), not this one. The CT puts w041 itself within 1–6 voxels of its sheet. All predictions come from one model, Reader v3. Other public 9 µm models (Reader v2, dense-native, ink_9um, v8-in) were noisier on this scroll in our tests.

Reproduce

The code in code/ is the code that ran in our lab repository; paths are relative to it.

python code/depthpair.py OUT --map=-4=predictions/w040-letters/readerv3_d-4.tif ... # see the script's docstring

File: reader-v3-screen/README.md

PHerc0306B Reader v3 inference screen

Download the release

This release preserves original Reader v3 prediction TIFFs for PHerc0306B, scan 20250521133212 at 8.64 µm. It contains 536 production sections / 1,072 TIFFs, both computational directions at depth 0, and 925 supplemental TIFFs. There are 1,997 TIFFs in 12 ZIP assets, totalling 11,812,543,798 bytes (11.81 GB). ZIP compression and packaging do not change the TIFF bytes or orientation.

Coverage

This is partial coverage, not whole-scroll inference. Height intervals below are half-open intervals in level-0 z voxels; winding IDs are local to each band.

Height interval Completed production sections TIFFs

2304–4608

4608–6912

6912–9216

9216–11520

11520–13824

Total 1,072

No completed production inference was found for z0–2304 or z13824–15898. Some covered bands have missing windings. The exact included and missing winding lists are in coverage.json. Missing lists compare each band to the campaign's w010–w129 range; they do not establish that

all those windings have valid geometry at every height. Supplemental windows and independent reconstructions do not fill these production coverage gaps. Earlier estimates of 240 sections and approximately 5 GB described only the original two-band campaign.

Model and production recipe

Model: domenicor046/reader-v3. Model revision: aee1d64bced4eb35546348f3d276b9e2a0b99c46. Checkpoint SHA-256: ea405417450abd8ace1b8ff79ebce3adb646c5e48ab95da46844d77efe984d8a. Production: an 18-layer rendered slab, depth 0, batch size 8, both directions, no TTA; overlap 0.5 with Hann blending. The model uses the recorded 17-plane context within that slab; no checkpoint context override was made. Villa commit: 0fb38c45b488e192566ea83ae36369cb6db92652. VC3D renderer commit: 41701aa0eaa1aa765523db3f9f972b5830abf549.

The images are uint8 prediction maps (255 represents probability 1), not human annotations or confirmed text. Production filenames call the reverse-layer prediction reading and the forward-layer prediction opposite. These are computational direction labels, not a biological guarantee of the ink face. Production maps retain the raw VC3D flat frame, with no image rotation. Supplemental sources have their own frame and orientation conventions, recorded in their provenance. Do not impose a single display flip on every source. Independent reconstruction pieces use their own local UV frames. They cannot be substituted for production winding maps using the winding label alone. Their source geometry is not included in these inference-only ZIPs.

Files and verification

files.csv enumerates every production TIFF: band, winding, depth, direction, dimensions, original byte size and SHA-256, ZIP asset and exact member name. supplemental-files.json records supplemental files, source groups and hash provenance. SHA256SUMS covers ZIP assets and the three metadata manifests.

All 536 production source archives were retrieved and their multipart and combined SHA-256 values checked against pre-existing verified retrieval acknowledgements. Every recorded production payload hash was rechecked; each retained TIFF's size and SHA-256 match those acknowledgements. TIFF dimensions were checked against render receipts and all production inputs identify the pinned checkpoint. Every release ZIP passed an integrity check and an exact TIFF membership check against the release manifests.

The original supplemental set contains 181 TIFFs from multi-depth/TTA runs and unchanged parent-model w040/w073 runs. Fine-tuned variants are excluded. Supplemental hash provenance differs by source: some files have pre-existing per-file hashes, while others have hashes computed during retrieval. Do not interpret the supplemental manifest as proof that every file had a preexisting independent hash. Additional source groups, where included, are described there with their own verification limits and geometry provenance.

The public download manifest contains outputs linked to the pinned, unchanged Reader v3 checkpoint. Auxiliary files with only producer-declared model identity and no recovered checkpoint hash, along with derived ensembles, are excluded from the clean public set. They remain in the private collection audit. Repeated TIFF bytes discovered across auxiliary archives are packaged once. The manifest describes the enumerated and verified sources, not a proof that every possible unnamed binary in the storage bucket has been identified as Reader v3 inference.

Only prediction TIFFs, curated provenance and licensing metadata are packaged. CT layers, masks, model checkpoints, human annotations and internal logs are outside this release.

Download selected predictions

The download helper requires Python 3 and only the standard library. From a checkout of this repository:

python3 code/download_reader_v3.py --band 6912-9216 --winding w040 --list python3 code/download_reader_v3.py --band 6912-9216 --winding w040 --direction reading python3 code/download_reader_v3.py --kind supplemental --list python3 code/download_reader_v3.py --kind supplemental --source w073b_rv3 --depth=-2 --direction reading

Without filters it downloads all production predictions. Use --kind all to include supplemental files. ZIPs are downloaded whole, cached, and checked against SHA256SUMS before extraction. Only selected TIFFs are extracted, and each is checked against its recorded byte size and SHA-256. An invalid cached ZIP is removed and causes a failure; run again to download a fresh copy. Incomplete downloads and failed TIFF extraction leave no completed output. Use --cache and --output to choose directories. The helper also works as a standalone script by fetching the release metadata.

ZIP archives can also be downloaded directly from the release. Each contains LICENSE-DATA.txt and curated provenance.json beside the original TIFFs.

Organization and supplemental source index

Production paths normalize the band and winding names. Supplemental paths keep the source group and original TIFF filenames; reconstruction pieces retain their piece paths.
